races.title: State Assembly, District 53
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Rafaela Romero
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 53 (Chino, Ontario, Pomona, Upland, Montclair). She says she grew up in Chino, lives in Ontario, and has worked in the grocery sector and in schools. She has not held public office. She advanced from the June 2026 primary.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists Reform California among her endorsements and voter-guide recommendations. Also listed: The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn, and the voter guides April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain.

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace, when she moved to or within California, or her job titles and employers. We found no record of her taking positions on data centers, development limits, property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice. Her stated priorities are affordability, education, public safety, and infrastructure, and they are general. She has not held office, so there is no record of actions in office.

cands.name: Michelle Rodriguez
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly for District 53 since December 2024. Born and raised in Ontario, California. Former healthcare administration worker (Inter Valley Health Plan, ProMed Healthcare Administrators) and school campus security officer. Has served on the state Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST). Succeeded her husband, Freddie Rodriguez.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, listed among her 2026 endorsements.
California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO, listed among her 2026 endorsements.
California Teachers Association, listed among her 2026 endorsements.
National Union of Healthcare Workers, listed among her 2026 endorsements.
Equality California and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund, listed among her 2026 endorsements.

cands.gaps: We could not find any bills she sponsored; the list on her Ballotpedia page was empty. We found no documented actions or stated positions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, donor money, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her campaign site lists broad priorities (safe neighborhoods, cleaner air and water, healthcare for all, jobs, women's equality, homelessness, schools) without specific commitments. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. Dates for her past jobs were not available. No controversies appeared in the sources we had.

qual.background: Assemblymember for District 53 since December 2024, with earlier work in healthcare plan administration, school campus security and local youth sports administration.
qual.why: She has held a legislative seat for about a year or two, which counts toward the middle-to-high range. Her prior career was in healthcare administration and school security, not law, policy or budget work. Her POST commission seat is an appointed board and adds nothing to the score.
